t:
(a) 
Paragraph (2) of subsection (c) of section 201 of the Federal Credit Union Act (12 U.S.C. 1781(c)(2)) is amended by striking out “reject” and inserting in lieu thereof “disapprove”.
 
    (b) Subsection (d) of such section 201 (12 U.S.C. 1781(d)) is amended to read as follows:

“(d) 
In the case of any Federal credit union whose application for insurance is disapproved, if such Federal credit union has annually transferred such a percentage of its gross income to its reserves as is required under section 116(a) and notwithstanding any reserving requirements established under section 116(b) of this Act, the Administrator shall nonetheless issue to such Federal credit union a certificate of insurance which shall be valid for a period of two years. The Administrator shall suspend or revoke the charter of any Federal credit union which has failed, upon the expiration of such two-year period of insurance, to file an application for insurance which is approved by the Administrator in accordance with subsection (c). A Federal credit union which is insured under this subsection for a period of two years is an insured credit union under the provisions of this title for such period of two years. The Administrator shall, having regard to the purposes of this subsection, make every reasonable effort to prevent the closing of any Federal credit union which is insured for a period of two years under this subsection and is found to be in financial difficulties, if he determines that with the technical assistance and management training and counseling authorized to be provided under this subsection there is reasonable assurance that such difficulties can be sufficiently resolved within such two-year period so as to minimize the expenses of the Fund. The Administrator shall offer technical assistance, management training, and management counseling to all credit unions whose application for insurance has been disapproved so as to enable the maximum number of such credit unions to meet the standards for insurance required by this title. In furnishing such technical assistance, management training, and management counseling, the Administrator may utilize moneys in the National Credit Union Share Insurance Fund as provided under section 203(a) of this title. The Administrator shall also encourage to the maximum extent feasible, that such technical assistance, management training, and management counseling be made available through State stabilization funds, similar funds, or similar State credit union organizations. The Administrator shall also encourage State Credit Union Stabilization Funds or similar funds to reimburse the Credit Union Share Insurance Fund for any insurance payments made on behalf of accounts at insured credit unions whose applications for insurance have been disapproved.”

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the references to State stabilization funds and State credit union organizations amount to coordination with outside entities. But the Administrator is only encouraging those bodies to provide assistance or reimbursement; they are not consulted before any federal decision. The rest of the section concerns applications for insurance, temporary certificates and technical assistance, and applications are expressly excluded from participation. There is no comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue.
fable.s: The Administrator shall also encourage to the maximum extent feasible, that such technical assistance, management training, and management counseling be made available through State stabilization funds, similar funds, or similar State credit union organizations.

opus.w: The State bodies mentioned are being encouraged to provide services and reimbursements. They are not being consulted before any federal decision, so this is not participation. The rest of the section deals with applications for insurance (which are excluded as benefit applications) and with the Administrator's own duties. It creates no comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking authority, or right to sue.
opus.s: The Administrator shall also encourage to the maximum extent feasible, that such technical assistance, management training, and management counseling be made available through State stabilization funds, similar funds, or similar State credit union organizations.
opus.b: 1. **Tempting reading:** The section mentions State stabilization funds and State credit union organizations, and it tells the Administrator to "encourage" them. That could look like coordination with outside entities. It doesn't meet the definition. The Administrator is only urging these groups to deliver technical assistance and to reimburse the insurance fund. No outside party is consulted before a federal decision is made. The insurance applications and charter decisions are applications for a benefit, which the definition excludes. Nothing in the section creates a hearing, a comment period, an advisory body, rulemaking, or a right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section outlines the Administrator's authority and duties regarding insurance certificates and technical assistance for credit unions. It does not require the Administrator to consult with or coordinate with any outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) before making decisions on insurance applications or charter revocations. The interactions described are unilateral actions by the federal agency (issuing certificates, offering assistance, encouraging state funds) rather than a participatory process involving outside input in the decision-making.
qwen_chat.s: The Administrator shall, having regard to the purposes of this subsection, make every reasonable effort to prevent the closing of any Federal credit union which is insured for a period of two years under this subsection and is found to be in financial difficulties, if he determines that with the technical assistance and management training and counseling authorized to be provided under this subsection there is reasonable assurance that such difficulties can be sufficiently resolved within such two-year period so as to minimize the expenses of the Fund.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the Administrator's duty to "encourage" State funds or offer "technical assistance" constitutes participation. However, these are actions taken by the federal agency towards outside entities, not a requirement for the agency to consult with or coordinate with outside entities *before* making a decision. The core decision-making process (approval/disapproval of insurance applications) is described as an administrative determination by the Administrator, without any mandated consultation with the public, states, or other outside parties. The "encouragement" is a unilateral federal action, not a participatory process.
